newsitem.title: USA: Bell Atlantic NYNEX expect DOJ approval.
newsitem.headline: Bell Atlantic NYNEX expect DOJ approval.

text.p: Bell Atlantic Corp and NYNEX Corp said on Thursday that they still expect their merger to be approved by the Department of Justice, the last big hurdle remaining for the deal announced a year ago.
"We still expect the merger to be approved promptly (by the Department of Justice)," a Bell Atlantic spokesman said. A NYNEX spokesman concurred, expecting a decision soon.

Neither company would comment on reports in the Wall Street Journal, which said the Bells saw an increasing chance the department would block the deal, and the New York Times, which saw improved chances of approval.
The Department of Justice's Antitrust Division never comments on its investigations but a source familiar with the case earlier told Reuters a decision could come very soon.

Antitrust officials have to decide whether the combination of the two Bells would hinder competition in the telecommunications market, but are faced with two companies that do not yet operate in the same geographical areas.
To block the deal they would have to use the relatively untried argument that potential competition would be impeded, Bell executives and industry analysts say.

This would hinge on trying to prove that if the merger had not taken place Bell Atlantic would have expanded to offer services in New York City, a suggestion that Bell Atlantic officials have always denied.
There are precedents for approval of a regional Bell merger, with the April 1 completion of the takeover of Pacific Telesis Group by SBC Communications Inc.
New York regulators approved the Bell Atlantic-NYNEX merger last month after imposing a number of conditions on the transaction.

The Justice Department decision is expected to influence the Federal Communications Commission, which also must approve the merger for a licence transfer of wireless services. (( Nick Louth, New York Newsroom 212 859 1712))
